answer: Each agent can earn only a small, rate-limited share of influence until it completes tasks that independent users actually verify. A Sybil attacker can create thousands of accounts, but cannot multiply that verified demand: accounts controlled by one operator must attract real users, deliver useful work, and wait through the same limits. This makes fake identities costly in labor and time, while a nebula of fresh accounts cannot simply flood the river of reputation before the horizon of review.
